deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematical text, formula or computation on this page. The image (folio 55v) shows only pencil sketches and a small blue stroke on lined paper. The paper has been folded horizontally and is damaged at the right edge.

(1) Upper half, centre. A roughly drawn circle, traced over two or three times. A firmly drawn horizontal segment runs from the left rim of the circle to a point just right of centre. At its right end are a small dot and a tiny loop or knot. A thin curve comes down from above the circle, from near the top of the sheet, and ends at this centre point. Outside the circle on the lower left is a separate short arc with a small hook at its lower end.

(2) Lower half. A short horizontal, slightly wavy double stroke (lens-shaped) sits on a ruled line, with a dot above it. To its right is a thin, irregular oval. Two points on its lower-left boundary are marked with small hatched blobs. A short straight segment leaves the upper of these two points towards the lower left. A faint line may extend further down and left.

(3) Upper left margin. A small blue crayon or pencil mark, probably a stray stroke or an archival or pen-test mark, with no mathematical content.

Possible context (this is my interpretation and is not certain). The facing page (55r) concerns the magnetic potential and Laplace's equation, with notes partly in Italian ('Potenziale magnetico', 'Strisciano', 'velocità'). That suggests Riemann's Italian period, c. 1863-65. Upper sketch: the radius-like horizontal bar with a thread-like curve descending to its inner end could be a suspended magnetic needle or bifilar/unifilar suspension seen from above, or a torsion element inside a circular casing or ring. It could equally be a schematic disc with a cut along a radius, a slit domain of the kind used for potential problems in a circle. Lower sketch: a closed curve with two distinguished boundary points and an attached segment could be a domain with two boundary points or electrodes, perhaps for a current-flow or potential problem. It could also be an unrelated doodle. Neither sketch carries labels, so no derivation can be reconstructed.

The following page is an administrative draft of c. 1862-64. It covers the telegraph link between the Göttingen observatory and the telegraph station, the longitude determination Göttingen-Altona by Klinkerfues, and the edition of the Hannover Gradmessung results with Schering. It also covers Riemann being charged to negotiate with General-Lieutenant Baeyer about the Mitteleuropäische Gradmessung. That page dates the bundle's physical sheets to the early 1860s, despite the bundle name '1853'.

Lower sketch: the short horizontal mark has a dot above it and appears lens-shaped (a double stroke) rather than simply wavy. The short line segment leaves the upper of the two marked points towards the lower left.
